premise: I invested $92,000 from my deceased husband’s pension into my niece’s vintage fashion boutique with a signed operating agreement granting me a 40% ownership stake; when a competitor offered $750,000 to buy it, my niece forged a dissolution document, paid me back exactly $92,000 claiming it was always a loan, and pocketed the sale—I proved the forgery, won the company’s intellectual property, rebranded it as ‘Second-Hand Vows,’ now run a thriving online resale shop, and she was court-ordered to work as my inventory sorter for 18 months wearing a lanyard that reads ‘Original Forger.’
